headline: 3 albino snakes rescued in Dhaka, Chattogram and Panchagarh
summary: Two albino checkered keelbacks and an albino monocled cobra were found across three districts, drawing significant attention on social media.
details: Three unusually coloured snakes—two albino checkered keelbacks and an albino monocled cobra—have been rescued in Dhaka, Chattogram, and Panchagarh within eight days.
The snakes' bodies appear yellowish, white, or pale pink, a result of a genetic condition called albinism caused by a lack of melanin pigment.
Experts explain that while albinism does not change a snake's species or venom status, it makes them more vulnerable to predators because they cannot camouflage effectively.
In Panchagarh, a checkered keelback was rescued after locals injured it with a spear; it is currently being treated by the Wildlife and Snake Rescue Team in Bangladesh (WSRTBD).
Other recent rescues include an albino monocled cobra in Dhaka's Demra and an albino checkered keelback in Chattogram's Chornelhat.
The WSRTBD has rescued five albino snakes across the country since 2020, most of them checkered keelbacks.
Researchers from Chittagong University and Chittagong Medical College Hospital urge the public not to panic or harm these rare animals due to their unusual colouring.
While albino snakes have long existed in Bangladesh, increased sightings are being reported due to the influence of social media and wildlife rescue groups.

headline_marked: AQI 171: [[Dhaka air quality world’s 5th worst]] on Thursday morning
headline: AQI 171: Dhaka air quality world’s 5th worst on Thursday morning
summary: The capital city's air is classified as 'unhealthy' according to IQAir, posing health risks to the general population.
details: Dhaka recorded an air quality index (AQI) level of 171 on Thursday morning, placing it fifth on the list of the world’s most polluted major cities.
The data, recorded between 8am and 9am on Nov 5, was provided by IQAir, a Swiss-based air quality technology and environmental organisation.
Pakistan’s Lahore topped the global list with an AQI of 338, categorized as 'hazardous', while Delhi ranked second with 270, classified as 'very unhealthy'.
Kolkata ranked third with an AQI of 201 and Karachi fourth with 174, both of which were also categorized as 'very unhealthy' or 'unhealthy'.
According to the US AQI classification, a score of 151-200 is considered 'unhealthy', which is the range Dhaka currently falls into.
An 'unhealthy' AQI reading means air pollution may pose health risks to everyone, with children, older adults and people with respiratory conditions being particularly vulnerable.
